## HAB-01 — all metrics, dates and cadence

The proposal correctly identifies distinct producers: computeStats monthly/year helpers; computeStreak; toggle; HabitRow totals/streak/weekly controls; HabitList today and all-week levels; HabitDetail single four cards/total/annual progress/badges; directory month/streak/Today; in-package Stats completedToday/month/rate/ranking/recent heatmap; All completedToday/month/rate/progress/remaining/width/day dots; MonthCalendar; and after-success recorded-event postStreak. These are not the separate Statistics product. Parent-source HabitDetail lines 130–147, 279–284, 462–477 and 568–575 corroborate independent count/rate paths; repairing computeMonthlyRate alone would miss them.

The proposed common selector is technically sound for decided cadences: strictly valid local civil days; inclusive explicit startDate; no invented createdAt-derived legacy floor; absent legacy cadence retains historical daily behavior; invalid explicit domain fields yield unavailable rather than daily fallback. Daily/weekday/weekend eligible populations derive from the named schedules plus the audit's due-cycle requirement. Future/pre-start/non-due data remains recoverable but never inflates count, denominator, width, badge or emitted streak.

Monthly rate uses completed eligible days divided by eligible days through min(displayed-month end,today); past months cover their full eligible range, future/zero-due months do not become 100% or NaN. Aggregates sum numerators and denominators, not individual percentages or habits × elapsed-day. A clamp is defensive, not an oracle. A partial result excluding unresolved weekly habits must be visibly incomplete. E1 annual progress retains 365/366 and current calendar-year meaning, with an eligible/future-filtered numerator; it is not silently renamed a due-opportunity completion rate.

Decided cadence streak walks consecutive due opportunities, respects inclusive start, skips rest days, and distinguishes unchecked due today from a missed past due opportunity. C1's current-day zero has a real accepted basis. No yesterday-count grace or skip allowance is introduced. Weekly streak and current weekly due status remain held below. Future/pre-start actions are disabled under the audit's offered future-disabled option; eligible past additions/removals are clearly historical corrections. Existing anomalous future bytes are not implicitly deleted.

Existing computeStats AC-STAT-5 includes 2026-12-25 at a 2026-05-23 reference and expects 3. The new audit requires that scenario to remain while the future key is excluded; removing the adverse fixture or calling its old green result acceptance would be wrong. The proposal explicitly preserves this distinction. Legacy daily positives remain useful, with new schedule/start/future/zero-eligible/mixed-population controls across every producer and visible state. Successful toggles emit exactly once after actual persistence; refused writes, noop, hydration and retries must not manufacture events.

## HAB-03 — latest-input durability, both-byte conflicts and lifecycle

The proposal accurately states current behavior: DiaryCard holds localValue and reports onDraftChange; HabitsModule captures text/identity/first baseline and flushes on local navigation or blur; current raw comparison refuses observed conflicts but does not provide a cross-tab transaction. The accepted mounted-page history cannot prove immediate close or process restart.

The per-change boundary is explicit and meets the original promise as a proposed invariant: every latest input must be durably captured before any saved/durably-retained acknowledgement. Debouncing only canonical consolidation is permissible after newest text is retained. The proposed journal carries full latest text, sequence, habit/month/owner/generation, base raw bytes and observed external raw bytes, not just hashes. It preserves empty-string edits. A matching readback precedes Draft saved, and canonical readback at sequence N cannot clear N+1. Canonical success plus journal-cleanup failure must not replay an older entry after reopen.

The proposed pre-acquired exclusive dataset/editor lease nested under account lifecycle ownership is a coherent candidate for synchronous per-change capture. Competing tabs can visibly refuse mutation. It is not already established by current accountCoordination/usePref: synchronous legacy writers, migration, global reset and export must join a reviewed protocol. No non-atomic localStorage lease/CAS fallback is allowed. Browser support, lease acquisition before input, release/revocation/liveness, crash release, every participating writer and reset/delete ordering remain impact-stage evidence requirements. A long-held shared lifecycle lease must not indefinitely prevent an authorized reset/delete: the future impact must specify bounded coordination and refusal/recovery; this report does not invent a timeout or new global guard.

Before canonical consolidation, revalidate captured owner/marker/tombstone/lease and compare exact source bytes. A changed source retains both local draft/base and newer external bytes; no silent whole-blob overwrite follows. Retry uses newest sequence under original identity; explicit reload/discard or a separately reviewed merge disposes of conflict. Both real tabs and missing-event interleavings are required because an event-driven synthetic fixture cannot prove serialization.

Storage failure after editing starts is honestly labeled Not saved, latest attempted text remains recoverable in memory, navigation/canonical overwrite is refused and real export/retry is offered. A forced close after failed durable capture is not waived as an acceptable lost-input case. Initial durability unavailability refuses edit acquisition. Full HAB-03 acceptance requires actual latest-input close survival under admitted storage and explicit fault handling; warnings alone do not pass it.

Owner A→B, locked owner, same-account epoch/generation change and reset/delete tombstones must fence stale callbacks, writes, downloads and seed effects. Recovery export/reset/deletion/migration must account for journal plus canonical state together. Existing account export enumerates registered account-owned generation keys and recovery exclusions; merely choosing a new logical key cannot prove inclusion. Export omissions need explicit scope/recovery paths. Global reset/delete completion requires lawful draft disposition, fencing and retryable cleanup receipt. The actual App.tsx departure order must be reviewed; legacy ConsoleLayout is insufficient. The proposal correctly locks host and shared lifecycle edits.

F2 remains per-habit/per-month. Required evidence includes typing before blur then actual tab close/reopen and full browser exit/restart, exact recovery downloads from disk, habit/month/view switches, latest retry during failure, stale callback, canonical/journal partial commit, both-tab conflict and lifecycle interleavings. Unit unmount and a hash-only export are insufficient.
